articles.title: How often to wash and replace your bed sheets, according to laundry experts
articles.summary: I talked to laundry experts to learn how often you should change and wash your bedding and when it’s time to throw them out for a new set.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like whether bath sheets are actually different from towels. There are so many different options online and in stores when it comes to bedding — the variety of pillowcases, flat sheets and comforters available makes it hard to know what to choose. What’s less confusing, though, is knowing that no matter what, your sheets need to be cleaned regularly to avoid stains, odors and damage. Knowing just how often you should wash your sheets and bedding is a little more obscure, plus, even if your bedding is technically clean, sometimes it may just be time to replace it. To find out how often you should change out and wash your sheets and when it’s time to replace them with a new set altogether, I spoke with laundry experts for their guidance. Keep reading to learn what they say, including how the rules change for pet owners who share the bed with their fur babies. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. How often should you wash your sheets? In general, you should change and wash your sheets around once a week, though this can depend on what type of bedding you’re referring to, according to Salvador Villarreal, the owner of laundry services company VIP Cleaners & Laundry. For things like fitted and flat sheets, once a week is standard, but for pillowcases, Villarreal recommends every three to seven days. Additionally, you should wash duvet covers every two to four weeks and comforters or duvet inserts at least every three weeks. If you have pets that sleep in your bed with you and/or are prone to allergies, you should be washing your bedding more often, according to Villarreal. Consider changing your sheets twice a week and cleaning your duvet covers and inserts every two weeks regularly and never stretching it to four. You can wash mattress protectors every one to two months overall. How often should you replace your sheets? While it may depend on the type of bedding and factors such as how often you’ve been washing them, you should replace your sheets every two to five years, according to Villarreal. If your sheets have stains that are hard to get rid of, the fabric is becoming thin, pilling, tears and has less elasticity, then it’s time to replace them, says Villarreal. “Duvet covers generally last longer since they protect the comforter underneath, while fitted sheets wear out first due to constant friction,” he says. Out of all types of bedding, though, fitted sheets should be replaced most often because of the friction they’re in contact with, according to Kim Romine, a fabric care scientist at Tide. The best products for washing and replacing sheets This simple and affordable product is an incredibly popular laundry detergent, mainly because it’s so effective according to the thousands of positive reviews shoppers have left for it. While it may seem just like baking soda in a box, it’s actually made with sodium carbonate and water (whereas baking soda you use for cooking and baking is technically sodium bicarbonate). Sodium carbonate, which some people use to make their own homemade laundry detergent (the brand even gives directions for this on the box), is more chemically basic than regular baking soda. The label actually lists several uses for washing soda, in addition to laundry, including cleaning pots and pans, surfaces and upholstery. Plus, many shoppers say they love using this product because it helps them save money on detergent. Just be mindful that you’ll want to refrain from using it on silk, leather or wool, according to the instructions on the box. Since I never use traditional bleach when I do laundry, I started using this powder oxygen bleach (which is different from highly corrosive liquid chlorine bleach) as an alternative. After using it a few times and soaking my clothing and sheets in it, I truly noticed a difference in the whiteness of my sheets. This powder, which is also available in tablet form, works well for cleaning and whitening clothing and bedding without the strong odors that come from traditional chlorine. Soaking definitely makes a huge difference and it has a “clean linen” smell to it that I enjoy. In addition to sheets, it works on canvas-based shoes, sports uniforms, shirts and socks, according to the brand. The Breeze Sheets are made from ultra-soft eucalyptus lyocell material that has a breathable feel, according to several reviewers.The lyocell fabric helps absorb and release moisture so that you don’t trap humidity under the sheets, according to the brand, so they’re less likely to make you sweat — which means less washing to get sweat stains out of the sheets. The set is available in several sizes and multiple stripe, plaid and floral designs. This popular mattress protector is available in twin sizes all the way up to California king, plus you can get it in multipacks. You can get it in five colorways, including brown, beige and white. It’s also available in a version for cribs and it’s entirely waterproof, according to the brand. It fits mattresses up to 17 inches tall, with shoppers confirming that it fits well and that it does a great job of keeping water out. It’s also machine washable in cold water. How do you wash sheets and bedding? Outside of washing your sheets regularly, it’s also important that you actually use the best techniques to keep them clean and in proper shape. It’s best to use warm water that is between 90 and 105 degrees Fahrenheit, to allow them to be cleaned thoroughly while also preventing them from becoming damaged, according to Villarreal. Another tip is to avoid overloading the washing machine to make sure clothes have room to move around. “Skip excessive detergent, since residue leaves fabric feeling stiff,” he says. “Tumble dry on medium heat and remove [them from the dryer] promptly to cut down on wrinkles and extend fabric life.” Below are some additional pieces of advice from laundry experts for changing, washing and maintaining sheets to help them last before having to replace them. It’s best to wash your sheets and bedding separately from other items, including towels, as this allows for more thorough cleaning and rinsing during the cycle, according to Romine. “Bedding specifically can accumulate sweat, body oils, skin cells, and personal care products over time. Washing these items separately can help ensure you aren’t overloading the wash with too much soil,” says Romine. “You also want to make sure you aren’t overstuffing the load with fabrics so they have enough room to move freely in the wash, allowing detergent and water to more effectively remove soils.”When it comes to bedding, watch out for things like fraying on edges and seams, as this is a sign that, rather than washing, you should simply throw out and replace the sheet, according to Romine. If you sweat a lot, (I’m looking at you hot sleepers), and your bedding is more likely to come in contact with perspiration, then you should change and wash your sheets more frequently than the general recommendation. Consider every few days versus once a week. Additionally, if you run hot while you sleep, consider cooling sheets like the Buffy Breeze Sheet Set might be a good investment for you. If you’re a pet owner and you allow your dogs or cats to sleep in bed with you, then you should also change and wash your bedding more frequently than once a week, according to Romine. “Pets can leave behind hair, dander, dirt, and other environmental debris that accumulate in bedding over time,” she says. “Likewise, bedding naturally collects dust and common environmental allergens that can build up.” Meet our laundry experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Salvador Villarreal is the owner of laundry services company VIP Cleaners and Laundry, based in San Diego.Kim Romine is a laundry expert and fabric care scientist at Procter & Gamble. *Any inclusion of Procter & Gamble products in this story was made independently of Romine, who we only consulted for shopping tips and guidance. We did not ask Romine for product recommendations. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home, kitchen, cleaning, laundry and more. I’ve written extensively about home cleaning and laundry, including how to whiten clothes without bleach, how to wash jackets and hats, the best products to restore leather clothes and furniture and more. For this article, I spoke with multiple laundry experts for their guidance on the best methods for washing and replacing bed sheets. articles.title: Falta de água:  40% de cidade do interior de SP é afetada | G1
articles.standfirst: Estação é responsável por diversas regiões de Rio Claro (SP) e o distrito de Assistência. Concessionária de energia foi acionada para realizar reparos na rede de alta tensão.
articles.summary: Estação é responsável por diversas regiões de Rio Claro (SP) e o distrito de Assistência. Concessionária de energia foi acionada para realizar reparos na rede de alta tensão.
articles.body:
Uma falha elétrica na rede de alta tensão que alimenta a Estação de Tratamento de Água “José Maria Pedroso” (ETA 1) provocou o desligamento temporário da unidade em Rio Claro (SP). A estação responde pelo abastecimento de 40% do município.

O Departamento Autônomo de Água e Esgoto (Daae) informou que acionou a concessionária de energia elétrica para efetuar os reparos necessários. A partir do conserto, as operações de captação, tratamento e distribuição de água serão retomadas.

Estação de Tratamento de Água “José Maria Pedroso” (ETA 1), em Rio Claro (SP) — Foto: Daae/Divulgação

A previsão inicial é que o fornecimento de energia na ETA 1 seja restabelecido no início da tarde desta quarta-feira (28). A partir daí, o abastecimento de água deve voltar ao normal de forma gradual ao longo da tarde.

As regiões e bairros atingidos pela paralisação temporária incluem:

Cidade Nova, Vila Paulista, Vila Alemã, Jardim Inocoop, Consolação, Cidade Jardim, Jardim Claret, Santana, Santa Cruz, Vila Operária e Jardim Mirassol;

O Daae destaca que os outros 60% do município são atendidos pela ETA 2 (“José Crespo”), que segue operando normalmente.

Recomendações e orientações após a religação

O órgão orienta que os moradores façam uso consciente da água, sem desperdícios, e lembra que a presença de caixa d’água nas residências reduz os impactos em interrupções do serviço.

Após a conclusão dos reparos na rede elétrica, a autarquia fará descargas na tubulação. O Daae alerta, no entanto, que a forte pressão no retorno da água pode ocasionar alterações temporárias no aspecto do líquido:

Cor escura: provocada pelo desprendimento de resíduos naturais (incrustações) retidos no interior dos tubos;

Aspecto esbranquiçado : causado pela formação de microbolhas de ar, que se dissipam em poucos segundos.

Segundo a autarquia, essas alterações pontuais não afetam a qualidade da água. Casos do tipo podem ser informados ao Daae pelo telefone e WhatsApp no número 0800-019-0505.

articles.title: Democratas condenam asilo do governo Trump a Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Integrantes do partido publicaram críticas nas redes sociais à possibilidade de o brasileiro obter asilo nos EUA.
articles.summary: Integrantes do partido publicaram críticas nas redes sociais à possibilidade de o brasileiro obter asilo nos EUA.
articles.body:
O Comitê de Relações Exteriores da Câmara dos Deputados dos Estados Unidos , ligado aos democratas, criticou a decisão do governo americano de conceder vistos ao senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e a seus familiares.

Em publicação nas redes sociais, o grupo comparou o tratamento previsto para o brasileiro à política migratória dos Estados Unidos em relação a pessoas que fogem de conflitos no Sudão e no Haiti.

“Nenhum asilo para pessoas fugindo da guerra no Sudão ou do conflito no Haiti, mas Rubio está estendendo o tapete vermelho para Bolsonaro. Aparentemente, fugir da violência não se qualifica. Negar os resultados eleitorais, sim”, afirmou o comitê.

➡️ O senador, derrotado nas últimas eleições presidenciais do Brasil, no domingo (25), viajou com a esposa e as filhas aos EUA. O avião pousou na Flórida na manhã desta quarta (28).

Comitê democrata critica governo dos EUA por concessão de vistos a Flávio Bolsonaro — Foto: Reprodução/X

Políticos democratas também publicaram críticas nas redes sociais à possibilidade de o brasileiro obter asilo nos EUA.

Em publicação na rede social Threads, o candidato democrata Isaiah Martin criticou a possibilidade de acolhimento do senador brasileiro nos Estados Unidos.

Martin chamou Flávio de “imigrante ilegal criminoso” e afirmou que os contribuintes americanos arcariam com os custos para proteger a família Bolsonaro e suas viagens pelo país.

"Agora, o contribuinte americano vai arcar com os custos para proteger sua família criminosa e suas viagens de luxo pelo nosso país", afirmou.

Outro democrata, o deputado Joaquin Castro, também questionou a possibilidade de Flávio obter asilo nos Estados Unidos.

“Perder uma eleição não é motivo para pedir asilo”, escreveu Castro no Threads. Na publicação, ele afirmou que o governo Trump estaria oferecendo um refúgio seguro ao senador, que é investigado no Brasil por suspeitas de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas, além de ter sido obrigado por decisão judicial a entregar os passaportes.

"O governo Trump deve explicações ao Congresso sobre seu papel em ajudar Bolsonaro a fugir do Brasil em desacordo com a legislação brasileira".

O Partido Democrata é o principal partido de oposição ao presidente Donald Trump, do Partido Republicano. As críticas ocorrem a menos de uma semana das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato, marcadas para 3 de novembro, quando os americanos vão eleger representantes para toda a Câmara e parte do Senado.

O candidato à presidência do Brasil, Flávio Bolsonaro, do Partido Liberal (PL), discursa após perder o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, em Brasília, Brasil, em 25 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Agustin Marcarian

Manifestação de Trump e do governo americano

As manifestações ocorreram após o Departamento de Estado dos EUA informar, na terça-feira (27), que concederá vistos a Flávio Bolsonaro e a seus familiares , permitindo a entrada do grupo no país. Até o momento, o governo americano não informou se os documentos já foram emitidos.

O governo argentino, em comunicado divulgado na madrugada desta quarta, afirmou que Flávio Bolsonaro entrou na Argentina junto da família na noite de terça. Esta foi a primeira confirmação oficial de que o senador deixou o Brasil, após um dia de rumores.

A saída ocorreu após o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinar, na noite de domingo, que o senador entregasse seus passaportes.

Nesta quarta-feira (28), Trump também afirmou que aprova a ida do senador aos Estados Unidos. Questionado por jornalistas, o presidente disse considerar os integrantes da família “boas pessoas” e voltou a criticar a eleição presidencial brasileira de domingo (25).

“Bem, eu aprovaria. Acho que eles são boas pessoas. A eleição foi muito estranha, e achei que foi terrível. Ela tem recebido avaliações ruins. Veja o que aconteceu com o mercado deles”, afirmou Trump.

Donald Trump na base aérea Andrews. — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

articles.title: Uso de adornos na saúde Paraíba: nova regra proíbe acessórios | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida da Secretaria de Estado da Saúde tem como objetivo prevenir infecções e garantir a segurança de pacientes e trabalhadores.
articles.summary: O uso de adornos na saúde Paraíba foi proibido em áreas de risco biológico para prevenir infecções e garantir a segurança de pacientes e trabalhadores do setor.
articles.body:
Trabalhadores da saúde na Paraíba — Foto: Beto Silva/TV Paraíba

A Secretaria de Estado da Saúde da Paraíba (SES-PB) publicou uma portaria que proíbe o uso de adornos por profissionais que trabalham em ambientes de assistência à saúde com risco de exposição a agentes biológicos. A Portaria n.º 828/2026/GS foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado desta quarta-feira (28).

A medida tem como objetivo prevenir infecções, facilitar a higienização das mãos e garantir a segurança de pacientes e trabalhadores. O documento foi assinado pelo secretário de Estado da Saúde, Arimatheus Silva Reis.

De acordo com as justificativas técnicas da portaria, o uso de adornos pode dificultar a higienização adequada das mãos, prejudicar o ajuste e a eficácia dos equipamentos de proteção individual (EPIs) e favorecer o acúmulo e a disseminação de microrganismos.

A restrição também busca reduzir as infecções relacionadas à assistência à Saúde (IRAS), que podem ocorrer durante a prestação de cuidados aos pacientes.

A medida tem como uma das bases a Norma Regulamentadora nº 32 (NR-32), do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego. A norma determina que empregadores proíbam o uso de adornos nos postos de trabalho com risco de exposição a agentes biológicos.

A portaria também se fundamenta em normas sanitárias e em legislações relacionadas à proteção da saúde, incluindo a Lei nº 8.080/1990, que regulamenta o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), e as diretrizes do Programa Nacional de Segurança do Paciente.

articles.title: 'Confusão sobre paradeiro de Flávio Bolsonaro': imprensa mundial repercute fuga de senador para os EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornais do mundo destacaram voo do senador e 3 familiares viajaram em jatinho particular da Argentina a Miami, nos EUA, entre terça e esta quarta (28). Eles cruzaram a fronteira com a Argentina por solo, e o voo não cruzou o espaço aéreo brasileiro.
articles.summary: Jornais do mundo destacaram voo do senador e 3 familiares viajaram em jatinho particular da Argentina a Miami, nos EUA, entre terça e esta quarta (28). Eles cruzaram a fronteira com a Argentina por solo, e o voo não cruzou o espaço aéreo brasileiro.
articles.body:
A imprensa internacional repercutiu nesta quarta-feira (28), a fuga do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), derrotado nas eleições presidenciais.

Veículos mundiais de grande circulação vêm cobrindo a história desde terça-feira, quando o jornal argentino Infobae divulgou que o senador brasileiro teria deixado o país. Uma confusão nas informações divulgadas por fontes de diferentes países à imprensa gerou notícias de que Flávio havia chegado aos EUA ainda na terça, porém, segundo o governo da Argentina, ele e sua família viajavam de avião nesta quarta, apenas.

Os jornais de diferentes países voltaram a repercutir nesta quarta a fuga para a Argentina e a viagem para o Equador.

A rede britânica BBC , que num primeiro momento havia confirmado a chegada de Flávio nos EUA, falou em "confusão sobre o paradeiro de Flávio Bolsonaro" nesta quarta após a Argentina informar sobre o cruzamento da fronteira na noite de terça.

Reportagem da rede britânica BBC sobre a fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro em 28 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/BBC

O veículo britânico mencionou que fontes deles afirmaram na noite de terça que Flávio havia aterrissado nos EUA.

"Há uma confusão sobre o paradeiro do candidato derrotado à Presidência do Brasil, Flávio Bolsonaro, depois que o Brasil cancelou seus passaportes e autoridades argentinas afirmaram que ele embarcou em um voo para o Equador. Fontes haviam dito à BBC nesta terça-feira que Bolsonaro tinha chegado aos Estados Unidos. No entanto, autoridades migratórias argentinas afirmaram posteriormente que ele havia cruzado a fronteira terrestre do Brasil com a Argentina na noite de terça-feira, no horário local", afirmou a reportagem.

O jornal português Público afirmou que "Bolsonaro fugiu da Argentina para o Equador e está a caminho dos EUA".

Reportagem do jornal Público, de Portugal, sobre a fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro em 28 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Público

"O jato privado em que Flávio Bolsonaro viajou da Argentina para o Equador, depois de ter fugido do Brasil por uma fronteira terrestre, partiu na manhã desta quarta-feira de Guayaquil, no Equador, para Miami, nos Estados Unidos (...) Tudo indica que seguem a bordo o ex-candidato presidencial e a família, que têm à sua espera vistos de entrada emitidos pelas autoridades norte-americanas", afirmou o jornal português.

O jornal espanhol El País falou no "escape" de Flávio do Brasil, repercutiu o anúncio do governo da Argentina sobre a entrada do senador e também deu destaque ao fato da cidade de Foz do Iguaçu e o estado do Paraná serem governados por políticos aliados ao bolsonarismo : General Joaquim Silva e Luna (PL) e Ratinho Júnior (PSD), respectivamente.

articles.title: Joanne Young: britânica relata 13 anos de abusos sob efeito de drogas | G1
articles.standfirst: Joanne Young contou que acordava com os olhos vendados e amarrada em depoimento à polícia, reproduzido nesta quarta (28) em tribunal que julga quatro homens acusados de abusá-la. História lembra caso da francesa Gisele Pélicot.
articles.summary: Joanne Young prestou depoimento em tribunal britânico contra quatro homens e o ex-marido, Philip Young, que admitiu ter dopado a esposa para facilitar os abusos.
articles.body:
Uma mulher do Reino Unido, drogada pelo então marido durante 13 anos para que desconhecidos mantivessem relações sexuais com ela, declarou que frequentemente acordava vendada e amarrada , em um depoimento feito à polícia e reproduzido nesta quarta-feira (28) em um tribunal britânico.

Em um depoimento de julho de 2024, Joanne Young descreveu o "padrão habitual" de suas relações sexuais com o marido, com quem era casada há duas décadas.

Segundo a mulher, eles costumavam ter relações sexuais depois de sair para beber com amigos ou após tomar uma última taça antes de dormir, e na maioria das vezes, ela "já estava em sono profundo quando ele iniciava a relação sexual".

A mulher explicou que acordava com os olhos vendados e amarrada, mas mal se lembrava de como tinha chegado àquela situação.

Mãe de três filhos, ela também descreveu uma noite de fevereiro de 2023 em que, após beber em um pub com amigos, foi dormir, mas acabou sendo acordada e descobriu que havia outro homem em seu quarto.

Na manhã seguinte, o marido lhe contou que vinha consultando "fóruns" e que havia "convidado alguém para vir em casa e nos ver tendo relações sexuais", relatou Joanne, acrescentando: "Fiquei muito perturbada e chocada ao saber que alguém esteve ali. Foi uma invasão absoluta, algo que eu jamais teria aceitado ou desejado".

Mohammed Hassan, um dos quatro réus, ao chegar ao Tribunal da Coroa de Winchester, no sul da Inglaterra — Foto: GLYN KIRK / AFP

Quatro homens estão sendo julgados em um tribunal de Winchester, no sul da Inglaterra , acusados de abusar sexualmente de Joanne Young, após o marido dela tê-los convidado a manter relações sexuais com ela sem o seu consentimento, entre 2016 e 2023.

Philip Young, de 50 anos, declarou-se culpado, no início deste ano , de múltiplos crimes sexuais - incluindo estupro, voyeurismo e a administração de uma substância com a intenção de atordoar ou subjugar - cometidos contra a então esposa, Joanne Young, que abriu mão de seu direito ao anonimato.

Dois dos quatro homens são acusados de estupro e outros crimes, enquanto os outros dois enfrentam acusações de agressão sexual, juntamente com Philip Young.

Os quatro homens, com idades entre 32 e 62 anos, que negam as acusações, permaneceram impassíveis no banco dos réus enquanto eram reproduzidas, no Tribunal de Winchester, as gravações em vídeo dos depoimentos de Joanne Young à polícia.

O caso de Joanne é bem similar ao da francesa Giséle Pélicot, drogada por mais de 10 anos pelo então marido, Dominique , para que mais de 70 homens a estuprassem. Ele foi condenado a 20 anos de prisão, pena máxima dada pela Justiça da França para o crime , em dezembro de 2024 (relembre no vídeo acima) .

articles.title: Comunidade terapêutica em Campina Grande é interditada por abusos | G1
articles.standfirst: Interdição foi feita pela Gerência de Vigilância Sanitária do município, após vistoria do MPPB.
articles.summary: A comunidade terapêutica em Campina Grande foi interditada após o MPPB flagrar agressões e uso irregular de medicamentos em pacientes no bairro Jardim Tavares.
articles.body:
Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB) em Campina Grande — Foto: Divulgação/Ministério Público da Paraíba

Uma comunidade terapêutica foi interditada, nesta terça-feira (27), em Campina Grande , por suspeita de maus-tratos contra internos. A interdição foi feita pela Gerência de Vigilância Sanitária (Gevisa) do município, após uma vistoria do Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB).

A comunidade funcionava no bairro Jardim Tavares, na Zona Norte. Segundo o MP, alguns internos informaram que teriam sido acolhidos de forma involuntária e estariam sofrendo agressões físicas e psicológicas praticadas pela direção e funcionários.

Além disso, estariam sendo forçados a tomar medicações à base de psicotrópicos fora dos critérios protocolares recomendáveis. Cada interno pagava a quantia de R$ 1,8 mil por mês.

Ainda no decorrer da inspeção, parentes e responsáveis foram chamados à comunidade terapêutica investigada para levar os pacientes para casa. Pelos relatos recebidos pela equipe de fiscalização, as famílias acreditavam que seus parentes recebiam tratamento compatível com os quadros clínicos que apresentavam quando recorreram a este tipo de ajuda.

articles.title: O jacaré que surpreendeu moradores ao atravessar ciclovia de lagoa | G1
articles.standfirst: O animal foi filmado nesta semana, em Três Lagoas. Pessoas acompanharam a travessia sem se aproximar do réptil.
articles.summary: O animal foi filmado nesta semana, em Três Lagoas. Pessoas acompanharam a travessia sem se aproximar do réptil.
articles.body:
Um jacaré foi filmado atravessando a ciclovia da Lagoa Maior, em Três Lagoas , na região leste de Mato Grosso do Sul, na noite de segunda-feira (26). O animal chamou a atenção das pessoas que estavam no local, que acompanharam a travessia mantendo uma distância segura. Veja o vídeo acima.

O vídeo foi gravado por Maycon Garcia, que passava pelo local com o irmão quando percebeu o jacaré caminhando de um lado para o outro da pista.

Ao g1, Maycon disse que já havia visto outros jacarés na Lagoa Maior, mas sempre dentro da água. Dessa vez, o animal estava parado perto da margem e começou a atravessar a ciclovia.

“Esse dia ele estava bem paradinho no canto e, quando passamos, eu e meu irmão reparamos que ele começou a caminhar, atravessando a pista de um lado para o outro. Foi quando resolvi gravar, mantendo a distância segura, por se tratar de um animal silvestre”, disse Maycon.

As imagens mostram pessoas observando o jacaré durante a passagem, sem se aproximar. A Lagoa Maior é um dos pontos de lazer de Três Lagoas, frequentado por moradores para caminhadas e atividades físicas.

🐊 Por que os jacarés ficam na água à noite?

Jacaré atravessa ciclovia em MS. — Foto: Maycon Garcia

Segundo o biólogo Marcos Ardevino, a temperatura da água pode ser mais favorável aos animais durante a noite, quando a temperatura do ambiente tende a cair. Como os jacarés são ectotérmicos, ou seja, dependem de fontes externas de calor para regular a temperatura corporal, eles podem permanecer na água para manter condições adequadas ao funcionamento do organismo.

Conforme o especialista, durante a noite a temperatura do ambiente geralmente fica menor que a da água. Os jacarés, por serem animais de sangue-frio, ficam dentro da água porque ela está mais quente e eles precisam desse calor para manter as funções fisiológicas.

articles.standfirst: Fundador da DeepSeek está entre os dez primeiros do ranking da Hurun China Rich List, que reúne 1.529 pessoas com patrimônio superior a R$ 4 bilhões.
articles.summary: Fundador da DeepSeek está entre os dez primeiros do ranking da Hurun China Rich List, que reúne 1.529 pessoas com patrimônio superior a R$ 4 bilhões.
articles.body:
Número de super-ricos na China atinge maior nível com ascensão de empresários de tecnologia — Foto: Getty Images

O número de super-ricos na China atingiu o maior nível já registrado neste ano, impulsionado pela entrada de empresários do setor de tecnologia na lista, entre eles o fundador da DeepSeek .

Segundo a Hurun China Rich List, divulgada nesta terça-feira (28), o país tem agora o recorde de 1.529 pessoas com patrimônio superior a 5 bilhões de yuans, o equivalente a US$ 750 milhões ou R$ 4 bilhões.

O total supera o recorde anterior, de 1.460 pessoas, registrado em 2021.

Liang Wenfeng, fundador da startup de inteligência artificial DeepSeek , estreou na sétima posição do ranking, com uma fortuna estimada em US$ 41,7 bilhões, cerca de R$ 223 bilhões.

Ele está entre os 263 novos integrantes da lista, provenientes, em sua maioria, dos setores de semicondutores, inteligência artificial e robótica.

A fortuna de Wenfeng aumentou após o lançamento do modelo de inteligência artificial R1, no ano passado.

Segundo Rupert Hoogewerf, principal pesquisador do Hurun Research Institute, responsável pela elaboração do ranking, a lista de 2026 reflete uma China com uma “economia em duas velocidades”: enquanto as fortunas ligadas à tecnologia disparam, as de setores tradicionais encolhem.

Entre os 100 primeiros colocados, 60% construíram suas fortunas em setores considerados estratégicos pela China. Essas áreas fazem parte de um plano lançado pelo país em 2015 para alcançar a liderança tecnológica em dez anos.

Fundador da ByteDance, Zhang Yiming voltou ao topo do ranking depois de ter ocupado a primeira posição em 2024. Sua fortuna é estimada em US$ 99,7 bilhões, cerca de R$ 533 bilhões, o maior valor já registrado na lista.

Ele superou Zhong Shanshan, fundador da Nongfu Spring e conhecido como “Rei da Água Engarrafada”.

A ByteDance, dona do TikTok e do Douyin, enfrenta pressões regulatórias crescentes em diferentes países. Apesar disso, seu chatbot de inteligência artificial, o Doubao, tem quase 420 milhões de usuários ativos por mês, número muito superior ao de seus concorrentes chineses.

Também aparecem entre os dez primeiros colocados Robin Zeng, fundador da CATL; Pony Ma, da Tencent; William Ding, da NetEase; e Chen Tianshi, da Cambricon.

A DeepSeek estaria perto de concluir uma nova rodada de investimentos de 100 bilhões de yuans, o maior valor já registrado na indústria chinesa de inteligência artificial. A operação elevaria o valor de mercado da empresa para quase 500 bilhões de yuans.

Na lista das mulheres mais ricas da China, elaborada pela Hurun, a primeira posição é ocupada por Zhou Qunfang, fundadora da Lens Technology, fabricante de telas sensíveis ao toque. Sua fortuna é estimada em US$ 18,9 bilhões, aproximadamente R$ 101 bilhões.

articles.title: Meet Joe Whale, the artist who became famous for doodling on a restaurant wall at 9 and now, at 16, explores 10 human emotions through paintings and sculptures in London
articles.summary: At 9, Joe Whale attracted attention for drawing on the walls of a restaurant in Shrewsbury, England.
articles.body: At 9, Joe Whale attracted attention for drawing on the walls of a restaurant in Shrewsbury, England. The young artist, known as the Doodle Boy, went on to work with international brands and create large-scale illustrations. At 16, he returned to Britain from Australia for Ambassadors of Feeling, his first major London solo exhibition, which opened at Truman Brewery on October 23, 2026. The exhibition featured a collection of characters representing different feelings and human experiences through paintings and sculpture. It marked another stage in Whale’s development, moving from the spontaneous doodles that first brought him attention towards a more structured exploration of emotion, technology and growing up.How Joe Whale went from a restaurant wall to an international art careerWhale first drew widespread attention when his doodles appeared on the walls of Number Four, a restaurant in Shrewsbury. His distinctive illustrations helped establish his public identity as the artist known as the Doodle Boy, and his work subsequently attracted collaborations with brands including Nike, Disney and Marks & Spencer. His projects have extended beyond commercial collaborations. Whale created an eight-foot-by-five-foot canvas doodle of Charles Darwin at Shrewsbury Library for Darwin200, a two-year global voyage aboard the tall ship Oosterschelde retracing the route of Darwin’s HMS Beagle. The voyage, which departed Plymouth in August 2023, also aimed to train 200 young conservation leaders.Whale illustrated Game of Scones (2021), written by Eric Luper and the first book in the five-book Bad Food series. His work has developed alongside changes in his life and surroundings. His family later moved to Adelaide, Australia, where he continued to build his artistic career. His practice has expanded beyond the characters and patterns associated with his early work, incorporating different formats and more deliberate themes. The London exhibition brought together several aspects of that development, presenting a collection built around emotional experiences rather than doodling alone.Ambassadors of Feeling: 10 characters, paintings and sculpturesAmbassadors of Feeling centred on 10 characters representing different qualities and experiences: Direction, Care, Humanity, Rebellion, Positivity, Peace, Imagination, Unpredictability, Impact and Awareness. According to the exhibition’s press materials, the show featured more than 22 newly created works, including large-scale acrylic paintings and sculpture. The characters gave Whale a framework for exploring feelings through visual forms. Rather than treating emotion only as an abstract concept, the exhibition translated it into a cast of recognisable figures, each associated with a particular theme. The collection invited viewers to consider how these qualities appear in their own lives.Whale has also applied his visual style to objects beyond traditional canvases. As part of outerwear brand Parajumpers’ 20th-anniversary project, he created a hand-illustrated Gobi jacket covered with his colourful characters. The project involved 20 artists reinterpreting the jacket, with their designs debuting at Milan Fashion Week in September 2026. The collaboration connected Whale’s illustration practice with fashion, demonstrating how his imagery could be adapted to a wearable format. It also placed his work within a broader collaboration between artists and a fashion brand. The jacket project was separate from Ambassadors of Feeling and should not be confused with the works exhibited in London. The Truman Brewery exhibition opened on October 23, 2026, and ran through October 25. It gave audiences an opportunity to see the new collection together, with paintings and sculptures forming the core of an exhibition organised around emotion and personal experience.What research says about drawing and children’s emotionsResearch has examined whether drawing can influence children’s moods, although these studies did not investigate Whale or his artwork specifically. In a study by Jennifer E. Drake and Ellen Winner, published in Cognition and Emotion in 2013, researchers examined how children used drawing to regulate their emotions. The researchers found that children’s moods improved more when they drew something unrelated to a negative experience than when they used drawing to express that experience. In the second study, which involved 123 children, researchers also compared drawing as a distraction with copying another person’s drawing. The findings suggested that the benefits depended in part on children actively creating their own drawings. A later study by Jennifer E. Drake, published in Frontiers in Psychology in February 2021, investigated how drawing could improve mood by distracting children from negative feelings. Across three studies involving children aged 6 to 12, the research examined the relationship between drawing, absorption and enjoyment. Drawing as a distraction produced greater absorption and enjoyment than drawing focused on expressing negative feelings.These findings offer one way to understand why drawing can be meaningful for children, but they should not be taken as evidence that every form of art improves emotional wellbeing. The studies examined specific drawing activities and short-term mood changes, rather than the long-term effects of an artistic career or viewing work in a gallery. For Whale, Ambassadors of Feeling brought emotion directly into the subject of his work. The collection’s characters gave individual feelings a visual form, extending the playful, immediate quality of his early doodles into a more structured body of paintings and sculptures. His career has grown from a moment of attention at a restaurant into collaborations across publishing, commercial art and fashion, with the London exhibition placing his exploration of human experience at the centre of his practice.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'The twin bond never dies': Vishal Batra opens up about life with brother Capt. Vikram Batra in new book
articles.summary: “Seva Parmo Dharma” - Service Before Self - is a phrase we often hear in war films, military stories, and patriotic speeches.
articles.body: “Seva Parmo Dharma” - Service Before Self - is a phrase we often hear in war films, military stories, and patriotic speeches. But behind every uniform is a son, a brother, a friend, and a family that learns to live with an absence no medal can ever fill. The courage of a soldier is remembered on the battlefield; the courage of those he leaves behind often continues quietly, for decades.Captain Vikram Batra remains one of the most enduring symbols of that courage. During the Kargil War in 1999, after the successful capture of the strategically crucial Point 5140, his now-iconic radio message - 'Yeh Dil Maange More' - came to represent the confidence and fighting spirit of a generation of Indian soldiers. The young officer remembered as 'Shershaah' would go on to become a legend, but legends too begin as ordinary boys in ordinary homes.It is that other side of the story that his twin brother, Vishal Batra, brings alive in 'Yeh Dil Maange More: Remembering Captain Vikram Batra, My Brother'. Beyond the battle honours and the stories of valour lies an empty chair at home, parents who lost a son, and a twin who shared not just childhood and memories, but even the months before birth with the brother he would one day have to mourn.Reading the book makes one pause before the word “martyrdom” and think about everything it contains - sacrifice on the frontlines, but also grief, pride, memory, and the lifelong responsibility of keeping a loved one’s story alive.That deeply personal perspective led to this conversation with Vishal Batra, not only about Captain Vikram Batra the soldier India reveres, but also Vikram the brother, the son and the young man behind the uniform.1. The book begins with your last meeting with your brother, Capt. Vikram Batra - the hug at Nizamuddin station on 09 March 1999. More than 27 years later, when you replay that morning in your head, what do you see now that you could not possibly have understood then?VISHAL BATRA: That hug would always be the freshest memory for me, it being the last meeting, and I have a crystal-clear image embedded in my heart and soul when we parted with that goodbye, not even having any premonition that it would be my last hug or seeing him alive physically.What I see now is the transformation he had in him post his Sopore days and commando course. He had become way too courageous, having experienced the counter-insurgency operations at Sopore and had lost the fear of death. (In the very first letter he wrote me from the battlefield on 16/June/1999, wherein he had mentioned that Life is at total risk and anything can happen here).When I look back now, all I see is the shared dream of him becoming a One Star General and travelling across all the critical formations of the Indian Army with him in his One Star Car, which was dreamt together (as I wasn’t recommended in the SSB thrice).2. India remembers Capt. Vikram Batra through extraordinary images - the Param Vir Chakra, ‘Shershaah’, Point 5140, Batra Top, and ‘Yeh Dil Maange More’. But this book seems almost determined to take the uniform off for a moment and give us Vikram - the human being. Is there a part of your brother that you feel the national legend has unintentionally hidden from us?VISHAL BATRA: The country knew him as Shershaah, the young bearded Captain who caught the fancy of Indians through his daredevil actions in Op Vijay and radioing the message “Yeh Dil Maange More”.There is nothing he had hidden, and the book talks about the Man behind the Uniform because for the nation, he was a legendary solider but back home, he was a doting brother, son, a friend and the book covers the journey of both of us as twin siblings who had knitted the dream of donning the Uniform together, shared dreams, our early childhood struggles and a journey that was weaved in a small town.The book talks about his last journey, wherein the Palampur city had a plan to welcome their son in an Open Jeep with the garlands post his first operation at Point 5140 (as everyone thought he would be back soon) but alas, it was coffin with wreath’s.3. When we speak about Kargil, we understandably celebrate victory and extraordinary courage. But your book also forces us to confront what victory costs - the empty chair at home, parents who lose a son, a twin who grows old alone. Do you think India talks enough about that second half of patriotism: the lifetime that families are asked to live after the soldier is gone?VISHAL BATRA: I personally believe that the trend is changing a bit now, wherein social media is really influencing the memories of our great soldiers who sacrifice their lives for the nation. The making of patriotic movies and Web series is adding colour to patriotism.But for family, it’s always the Unit/Paltan which stays in touch and ensures that the sacrifice is never forgotten and the soldier is revered. For the family, no amount of comfort can ever fill the deep loss, and the void that gets created stays until we die.4. There is something particularly haunting about the fact that Capt. Vikram Batra's final letter reached you only after he was martyred. Has there ever been a moment in the last 27 years when you went back to Capt. Vikram’s final letter because you needed your brother’s advice?VISHAL BATRA: For me, life took a complete 360 turn when we heard of his martyrdom. It was like I lost the most important limb of my body. Being identical twins, we had numerous shared dreams of his Army life and my corporate life, which were shattered to a tee.But he had become such an inspiration that whenever I was in crisis or a catch situation, I logged onto his last interviews and asked myself, if he could be so daredevil and courageous in the thick of a bloody war, why should I not be moving forward.He always knew that I had all the talent (as I was ahead of him in studies) and competence to do well, so I always resort to his last letter dated 05 July,1999 (written just two days before he attained martyrdom) wherein he had written: “Aare Yaar! Don’t take tensions and keep doing your bit faithfully and sincerely. Definitely, God is looking at everyone, and he will definitely reward one day. You have all the potential to do anything, and I am sure you will definitely rise very high in your life. Take life in its stride; you will realise you are the happiest person.”I continue to believe that he is guiding me all through from the heavens above, as the twin bond never dies. We had the blessings of Almighty to spend those nine months extra in our mother’s womb wherein our bond would always be eternal.5. Regarding the letter, you received Capt. Vikram Batra’s final words when there was no longer any possibility of replying. If there was a chance, what would you have written back to him?VISHAL BATRA: Alas, I so bloody wish I had one more opportunity to write him back; all I would have written is that he has become a National Hero, and we all are so desperately waiting for him to come back and would love to hear the story of his courageous and daredevil actions from him.All I would have written him is that the day is not far when he would take the honour of participating every year in the 26th January Republic Day Parade at Rajpath and salute the honourable President in an Open Gypsy.6. Kargil came only months after the Lahore Declaration and barely a year after India and Pakistan had openly demonstrated their nuclear capabilities. Looking back as the brother of somebody who paid the ultimate price, what lesson do you think Kargil still holds for India about peace with Pakistan - about where dialogue must continue, but where trust must end?VISHAL BATRA: Kargil was just not the first incident, and we had seen the two earlier wars. So I believe that it would be naive to think that Pakistan can ever be trusted.The world also knows that Pakistan is a rogue nation and home to globally recognised terror groups, but at the same time, we also know that it is largely at their political leadership level. So efforts to reach a consensus must continue to find a peaceful solution to the lingering disputes in the larger interest of peace in the subcontinent.7. At a time when the youth feel increasingly disillusioned with the country, Captain Batra represented an extraordinary sense of 'Seva Paramo Dharma,' without expecting anything in return. As his brother, what message would you give the youth today?VISHAL BATRA: The message I have for the youth is that we don’t always have to don the uniform to become patriotic. We are all a part of this beautiful country, which has a rich legacy in its culture and diversity. And every step that you take, be it keeping the country clean and safe, respecting the elderly, respecting cultural diversity, maintaining brotherhood, or adding professional competence that can take this country ahead, do that within your Domain. Keep the nation in mind because any country is known by its citizens and its culture.

When it goes unchecked, taxpayers finance improper payments while eligible Americans and legitimate programs compete for what remains. Every dollar Trump stops from reaching a fraudster is one taxpayers do not have to replace through higher taxes or additional borrowing. President Trump’s record makes the connection clear: Affordability begins with enforcing the law and protecting the money families already earned. While Democrats burn time and resources making the midterms a referendum on President Trump, Republicans must double down on his accomplishments and show how America is safer and government is more accountable than it was two years ago. articles.title: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family land in Miami after fleeing Brazil
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election...
articles.body:
APTOPIX Brazil Election Flavio Bolsonaro

MIAMI (AP) — Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and fled the country.

In a circuitous journey, Bolsonaro left for Argentina on Tuesday with his wife and two daughters, then traveled to Ecuador, according to Argentina officials and flight data. The 45-year-old senator, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, visited the White House in May, and the Trump administration approved U.S. visas for him and his family this week.

Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula before returning to Brazil three months later.

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court, accused of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. The court had ordered him to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday. It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said late Tuesday he also has an Italian passport.

Dressed casually in a dark polo shirt and flanked by his wife and two daughters, Bolsonaro stepped out of the plane shortly after it landed in Miami about 9:30 a.m. EDT. Florida is home to the largest population of Brazilians in the U.S.

The family fled Brazil late Tuesday, entered Argentina via a border checkpoint and quickly boarded a private charter plane, Argentinian immigration officials said.

Flightradar24 showed the plane believed to be carrying Bolsonaro landed in Guayaquil, Ecuador, about 4 a.m. local time, then took off minutes later for Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport.

Before the family landed in Florida, Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, spoke to dozens of supporters outside the presidential residence in Brasilia.

"I regret that he left Brazil, because he could have stayed here and proven that the accusations are not true," Lula said. "This act of leaving Brazil is shameful."

Bolsonaro's route through Argentina could deepen diplomatic tensions between Lula's government and Argentine President Javier Milei, another Trump ally who traveled to Brazil to assist in Bolsonaro's campaign.

Representatives of Brazil's government didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump questions Brazilian election results

Trump has said Bolsonaro is welcome in the U.S., calling him and his family "fine people."

"The election was really strange, and I thought it was terrible," Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, on Tuesday. Earlier, Trump also said, without evidence, that the election was "rigged."

Leaders around the world and the Organization of American States have endorsed the result and congratulated Lula, who was reelected by a margin of about 4.4 million votes in the second and final round.

The U.S. has imposed double-digit sanctions on Brazil, which boasts Latin America's largest economy. Lula has championed Brazil's long tradition of nonalignment, cultivating ties with competing powers. His government has deepened trade ties with China and sought greater global influence through BRICS , a group of emerging economies.

Bolsonaro visited his father, who is under house arrest, before leaving Brazil

Brazil's Supreme Court ordered the defeated candidate to surrender his Brazilian passports Monday. In a video, he said he received the order outside the home where his father is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for his attempted coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula.

A Brazilian diplomat who was not authorized to speak about the matter publicly told The Associated Press that Bolsonaro used an Italian passport to enter Argentina and that Brazilians leaving the country via a land border are not scrutinized by Brazilian authorities.

The diplomat said Brazil's federal police were not monitoring Bolsonaro when he left his home in Brasilia because the Supreme Court had not issued a warrant for his arrest.

Flávio Bolsonaro said in a video Monday that he was attempting to organize opposition to the election results among his congressional colleagues. His eight-year term as a senator expires Jan. 31, 2027.

Brazil's Supreme Court is investigating Bolsonaro for allegedly using a sports betting company to launder fraudulent deductions from government pensions paid to senior citizens. In a separate case, he is accused of accepting millions of dollars from a disgraced banker . Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing.

Mauricio Savarese reported from Sao Paulo.

articles.title: Israeli right makes provocative statements as election votes are counted
articles.summary: Netanyahu and Smotrich rail against Arab voters as rival political camps face an uncertain path to power.
articles.body:
Senior figures on Israel’s right have made a series of provocative statements about Arab voters, alleged attempts to steal the election and plans to establish Jewish settlements in Gaza.

The remarks came during Tuesday’s election and after exit polls suggested Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing alliance had suffered a setback.

With neither major political camp securing a clear majority , Arab-led parties could play an important role in deciding who forms the next government.

Speaking early on Wednesday at his far-right Religious Zionism party’s election headquarters in Jerusalem, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich dismissed opposition celebrations and promised to preserve the expansion of settlements in the occupied West Bank, which are considered illegal under international law.

He said his political opponents would not reverse the government’s settlement “revolution”, declaring: “Jewish settlements will be established in Gaza.”

Israel dismantled its settlements in Gaza in 2005.

Earlier on Tuesday, Smotrich warned on Facebook that voter turnout was unusually high in Arab communities and left-wing strongholds, without providing supporting figures.

He claimed that failing to mobilise right-wing voters could allow “terror supporters” to enter government.

Netanyahu, who leads the right-wing Likud party, made similar appeals during voting, warning that Arab voters were rushing to polling stations and that an opposition victory would threaten Israel’s Jewish character.

He also accused three senior figures from Ra’am, an Arab-majority party, of attempting to steal the election.

Police confirmed they arrested three people on suspicion of voter bribery, but there was no indication they held senior positions in Ra’am.

Transportation Minister Miri Regev, also from Likud, echoed the unsubstantiated election theft allegations in a post on X on Tuesday. “They’re trying to steal the elections and the country from us,” she said . “It’s either the right or Palestine.”

British-American political scientist Dov Waxman told Al Jazeera that Netanyahu’s plan after the inconclusive election result will likely be to “hammer home the message” to the Israeli public that a governing coalition that consists of Arab parties is “illegitimate”.

Arab political leaders condemned Netanyahu’s election-day messages as racist and inflammatory.

Al Jazeera correspondent Nida Ibrahim, reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, said Netanyahu’s bloc of right-wing and religious parties was projected to win 56 seats, with 84 percent of ballots counted, short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament.

She said Mansour Abbas, the leader of Ra’am, claimed he had received approaches from both Netanyahu’s Likud and the opposition camp led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief who heads the Yashar party.

articles.title: China denies Taiwan’s claim it orchestrated attack on comedian who mocked Xi Jinping
articles.summary: Taiwan ​is “provoking confrontation,” a Chinese spokesperson said, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese comedian.
articles.body: Taiwan ​is “provoking confrontation” and stirring anti-China sentiment, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese comedian whose shows mocked Beijing. Taiwan, the democratically governed island ⁠that China claims as its own territory, has accused Beijing of trying to use “transnational repression” against people in Taiwan the Chinese government views as separatists or politically suspect. Taiwan’s government says China was behind last month’s attack on comedian Huang Yi-hao, who ⁠satirized Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speaking at a ​regular ⁠news conference in Beijing and asked about the incident, Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson Chen Binhua dismissed Taiwan’s accusations as a fabrication by ⁠its ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). “The so-called transnational repression narrative is essentially a way ​of ⁠promoting Taiwan independence and peddling a ‌two-state theory, and it is trotted out every time there is an election on the island,” he said, referring to next month’s local elections ‌in Taiwan. “The DPP fabricates all kinds of pretexts ‌out of thin air, maliciously smears the mainland, stirs up anti-China sentiment, and provokes cross-strait confrontation, all in an attempt to win political power by misleading the Taiwanese public,” Chen said. This ⁠is a “tired routine” repeated year after year, he added. Taiwan prosecutors said the defendants, whose full names it has not provided, were paid to fake a car accident and “break the arms and legs” of Huang so he could not perform, though in the end he was only lightly injured. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, speaking at a weekly DPP meeting later on Wednesday, said “transnational repression” ‌was a tool China could use to erode public trust in ​the island’s democratic system. “China’s aims in interfering in Taiwan’s elections include not ‌only attempting to directly change ⁠voting results, but also spreading false information, intensifying social divisions, and inciting ⁠group hatred,” he said. Other China critics in Taiwan have also been attacked, including Hong Kong ‌singer and activist Denise ​Ho in 2019. Taiwan’s government rejects Beijing’s ‌sovereignty claims, saying only the Taiwanese ​people can decide their future.

articles.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Supreme Court must take Herridge case and protect reporters' sources
articles.summary: Former Fox News investigative reporter Catherine Herridge has asked the Supreme Court to hear an appeal centered on her refusal to reveal her confidential sources.
articles.body: Not long ago, former Fox News investigative reporter Catherine Herridge began a painful daily ritual. With her oldest son for support, she walked to the mailbox at the end of her street and dropped an envelope into the mail. It contained a check for a daily fine of $800 that she was ordered to pay to coerce her into revealing her confidential sources in a national security story that aired on Fox News in 2017. The money came from the college funds of her two children. As Herridge drained the savings of her military family, an alleged former colonel in the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) was demanding that a court increase the daily fine to $5,000. A court later rescinded the fines, but they will be reimposed unless the Supreme Court takes Herridge’s case and reverses the lower courts. Yanping Chen led a school called the University of Management and Technology (UMT) in Northern Virginia, which catered to U.S. service members. According to investigators and experts, Chen’s past in the Chinese military suggested that UMT posed a national security danger, including by potentially gathering information on military personnel participating in its programs. The Department of Justice declined to prosecute Chen. Nevertheless, after Herridge's investigative report, the government terminated its contracts with UMT because it considered the school a national security risk. $800-A-DAY PENALTY THREATENS TO BLEED REPORTER DRY AS EXPLOSIVE LEGAL FIGHT HEADS TO SUPREME COURT In her investigation, Herridge published details that directly contradicted Chen, who denied being a colonel in the PLA. Herridge showed photos in her report of Chen in her PLA uniform, and a whistleblower said on camera that UMT collected information on the military training of its students, and it was all remotely accessible from China on UMT’s computers. All of that would seem to be the makings of a Pulitzer, not a court sanction. It is not uncommon for journalists to be sued by aggrieved subjects of their stories for defamation or other civil claims. Those cases are routinely rejected given the protections for the press under First Amendment cases like New York Times v. Sullivan, requiring a higher burden of proof from public figures suing the media. However, Chen did not sue for defamation. She did not even name Herridge as a party. After all, Herridge is not being accused of writing anything false. Instead, Chen latched onto a clever tactic. The alleged PLA colonel sued under a law that does not exist in China: the Privacy Act. The Privacy Act regulates the government’s collection, storage and use of private information, and includes a private right of action for citizens to sue for abuses or violations. She accused government officials of violating her privacy by serving as confidential sources to Herridge. Her counsel then subpoenaed Herridge and demanded that she reveal her sources. She refused. What is particularly alarming about this case is that the Privacy Act complaint was anemic and dubious from the outset. Much of what Chen references in her filing was available in the public domain. For example, Stephen Rhoads, a whistleblower and former UMT employee, was an FBI informant in the case and said publicly that Chen had admitted to him that she had been a PLA colonel and told him to lie about that fact when he was called to testify before a federal grand jury. Any viable claim is primarily based on the photos. However, given all the other information in the public domain, it would have been difficult to argue that the photos caused Chen substantial harm. Her association and alleged hidden former rank as a PLA colonel led the government to take action against her and UMT. However, Herridge had to litigate her claims of journalistic privilege in Washington, D.C. Despite being the single most important jurisdiction for investigative reporting, the federal courts in D.C. have long followed a more permissive approach to forcing the disclosure of confidential sources. Not only did Herridge find herself in a less-than-optimal circuit, but her supporters also raised concerns about the assigned judge. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper, an Obama appointee, is the husband of respected attorney Amy Jeffress, who has been referenced in past Herridge stories and represents clients who have been subjects of her investigative reporting. In 2023, Judge Cooper ordered Herridge to identify her confidential sources. She refused. Cooper then held her in contempt and imposed a crippling $800-a-day fine. The D.C. Circuit later upheld his order. When Herridge asked the Supreme Court to intervene and stay the D.C. Circuit’s mandate, it also declined (though Justice Brett Kavanaugh indicated that he would have granted relief). She is now back on a final appeal, hoping four justices will let her present her case. They should grant this petition and address the morass left by the ill-considered 1972 precedent in Branzburg v. Hayes. One appellate judge summed up the view of many by saying that the standard in the case is "about as clear as mud." (United States v. Sterling, 724 F.3d 482, 523 (4th Cir. 2013) (Gregory, J., dissenting)). The result has been decades of dangerous ambiguity in an area that needs clear rules. Where circuits such as the First Circuit apply a balancing test that allows for greater contextual resolutions, the D.C. Circuit applies a standard that is easy to satisfy. Chen needed only to show that (1) the source is central to her case and (2) she has exhausted other avenues of discovery. That test could have allowed Nixon officials to force Watergate reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein to disclose the identity of Deep Throat as a Privacy Act violation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Herridge's counsel has argued that the Court should adopt the more protective standards applied outside of Washington or create a new standard. One suggested approach is to allow a judge to consider whether a case is likely to survive a motion for summary judgment before ordering such disclosure. In this case, Chen is unlikely to secure any relief based solely on the photos, given the rest of the publicly available information about her past in the Chinese military. Ironically, Chen is seeking to use rights that are denied in China in a way that would seriously undermine the protections of a free press in this country. However, if she thought ruinous fines would force disclosure of such sources in a national security case, she tangled with the wrong reporter. Herridge has long been a champion of journalistic privilege, even when fighting news organizations. Years ago, I disclosed in a column how CBS News seized Herridge's files containing confidential source information after she left the network. Herridge refused to yield and forced the network to surrender the files. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Herridge is not asking for immunity. She is seeking to establish a fair standard, so a court can balance interests in cases such as hers. Chen was able to repurpose the Privacy Act as a way to circumvent press protections in areas like defamation. It would be particularly concerning if an alleged former colonel in the PLA whom DOD found to be a national security threat could claim privacy violations to force the disclosure of national security sources. There is ample ground here to strike a reasonable balance, but the Court must first accept review in Herridge v. Chen. Jonathan Turley previously worked for CBS News and currently works at Fox News as a legal analyst. His views do not necessarily reflect those of those networks. articles.title: Netanyahu or Eisenkot? Can you form Israel’s next coalition government?
articles.summary: Israel has only ever been governed by coalitions. Can you put one together that reaches 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats?
articles.body:
Israelis voted on October 27, but there appears to be no clear winner .

The next government, like every government in Israel’s history , will have to be a coalition.

The question now is who can secure at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats to form a government and become Israel’s next prime minister.

Al Jazeera has built an interactive tool that lets you test different combinations of parties. Start with any of the four exit polls or enter your own seat numbers. Then add parties until your coalition reaches 61 seats. You can add an entire bloc at once or select parties individually.

Initial counting by the Central Elections Committee put Likud ahead as the largest single party, with 27 seats.

Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 54 seats, against 50 for Eisenkot’s.

Four exit polls published on election night showed how close the race is.

Kan 11 and Channel 13 put Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc and Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc level at 51 seats each. Channel 12 gave Netanyahu 52 seats to Eisenkot’s 49, while Channel 15 was most favourable to the incumbent, projecting 55 seats for Netanyahu’s bloc against 49 for the opposition.

Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, has 120 seats. Parties win seats in proportion to their share of the national vote, provided they clear the 3.25 percent threshold to enter parliament.

A government needs the support of at least 61 politicians to secure a majority.

Neither of the main blocs has reached that number in the exit polls or the initial count. The next step is to find enough parties willing to join forces to make up the difference.

Why is forming a government so difficult?

The Arab-led parties Ra’am and the Joint List could hold the balance of power, with exit polls putting their combined support at between 16 and 19 seats.

But the political obstacles are considerable. Netanyahu has described a coalition with Arab parties as “shameful”, while leading figures in the Jewish-led opposition have also ruled out governing with them.

That leaves potential coalitions that may work on paper but face serious political barriers .

Netanyahu’s bloc spans Likud, the ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism, and the far-right parties Religious Zionism, led by Bezalel Smotrich, and Otzma Yehudit, led by Itamar Ben-Gvir.

Eisenkot’s opposition bloc includes his Yashar party, the Together list associated with former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beytenu and Yair Golan’s Democrats.

Once the results are certified, the president gives the mandate to the member of the Knesset considered most likely to assemble a majority.

That politician has 28 days to form a government, with a possible extension of up to 14 days. If they fail, another lawmaker can be given a chance. If no one can form a government, Israel may have to hold another election, as it did repeatedly between 2019 and 2022.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, with 19 years in office across three stints, remains caretaker prime minister while coalition negotiations unfold. He is also standing trial on corruption charges, which he denies.

Official results are due on November 4. Negotiations to form a government could take considerably longer.

articles.title: Giant statues of pharaoh with Moses link discovered after farmer finds inscribed stone
articles.summary: An Egyptian farmer's cucumber greenhouse discovery led archaeologists to unearth two colossal statues believed to depict Ramses II, the pharaoh linked to Moses.
articles.body: An Egyptian farmer tending to his cucumbers stumbled upon an ancient stone that led archaeologists to a much bigger discovery. They found the remains of two colossal statues believed to depict Ramses II, the pharaoh some scholars believe may have confronted Moses in the biblical Book of Exodus. The finds were announced by the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities earlier this month. ANCIENT EGYPTIAN SETTLEMENT DISCOVERED FROM ERA THAT FUELED EXODUS DEBATE The farmer found the inscribed stone while working in a cucumber greenhouse on his property in the village of Behbeit El-Hagar, according to Egyptian news outlet Youm7. The man then alerted local archaeological authorities, who inspected the site and uncovered the remains of two statues during subsequent excavations, ministry officials said. "One of the statues has been identified as depicting King Ramses II, while the other is also believed to represent the same pharaoh," the translated statement read. "The mission additionally discovered a pink granite block bearing hieroglyphic inscriptions that include several of the king's royal titles." Ramses II, who was born in 1303 B.C., was among the most powerful and influential pharaohs of ancient Egypt's New Kingdom period. ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNEARTH ANCIENT TREASURE CACHE AT BIBLICAL CITY CONNECTED TO GENESIS Some scholars have suggested that Ramses II was the pharaoh described in the Book of Exodus, although the Old Testament does not identify the ruler by name. In the biblical account, the pharaoh refuses Moses' demands to free the Israelites, leading to a series of devastating plagues. Ramses II died in 1213 B.C. The first statue features a colossal head of Ramses II measuring more than 5 feet tall, officials said. The pharaoh is depicted wearing a double crown, symbolizing the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt, while an inscription on the statue's back pillar bears one of his royal names. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Archaeologists estimate the original statue, including its base, may have stood nearly 28 feet tall. The second statue, also believed to depict Ramses II, measures nearly 8 feet long and is missing its legs and base. "The statue's head was also uncovered, with its facial features still clearly visible and well-preserved," officials said of the second statue. "These features closely resemble those of the first statue." Excavations and archaeological studies at the site are ongoing, officials added. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "These investigations are expected to help researchers develop a clearer understanding of the two statues, the area's history and its architectural development during ancient Egyptian times," the statement concluded. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The discovery is the latest in a series of archaeological finds shedding new light on the ancient Egyptian ruler. In a similar discovery, archaeologists in Egypt unearthed a massive statue believed to depict King Ramses II at a Nile Delta site northeast of Cairo earlier this year.
